name: BlinkDB
tagline: Berkeley AMPLab/MIT approximate query engine on Spark/Shark returning answers with error bars from samples.
description: BlinkDB was a research system from UC Berkeley's AMPLab and MIT, led by Sameer Agarwal, that answered HiveQL aggregate queries on very large data in seconds by running them on pre-built stratified samples and returning results with confidence intervals. It chose which samples to build from past query workloads and data distribution within a storage budget, and at query time picked a sample to meet a user-specified error or response-time bound. Built on Shark and Spark and compatible with Apache Hive, it was described in a EuroSys 2013 paper and released as alpha code supporting AVG, SUM, COUNT, VAR and STDEV. Development stopped in early 2014; its ideas fed into later approximate query processing work and sampling features in modern engines.
statusNote: AMPLab research prototype (2012-2014); alpha releases only and no commits since February 2014.
basedOn: Shark / Apache Spark and Apache Hive

scale.notes: Ran on Spark clusters; evaluated on multi-terabyte datasets in the research paper.

strengths: Bounded-error or bounded-time answers on very large tables
Workload-aware stratified sampling within a storage budget
Influential, well-cited design for approximate query processing
weaknesses: Alpha-quality code tied to Spark 0.9 and Shark, both long obsolete
Only aggregates with closed-form error estimates were supported
useCases: Studying approximate query processing and sampling-based analytics
Teaching trade-offs between accuracy and latency
